rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Concept 5: Connection between Stefan-Boltzmann Law and other topics  ·  Key Formula 5: Important relation in Stefan-Boltzmann Law  ·  ❌ Doubling the temperature doubles the radiated power. ✅ Because of the $T^4$ dependence, doubling the temperature increases the power by a factor of $2^4 = 16$, not 2. This dramatic sensitivity is a hallmark of the Stefan-Boltzmann law.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The $T$ in the Stefan-Boltzmann law can be in Celsius. ✅ The temperature MUST be in Kelvin. At 0°C (273 K), the radiated power is NOT zero — it is $\sigma(273)^4 \approx 449$ W/m². Using 0°C would incorrectly give zero.  ·  ❌ The Stefan-Boltzmann law applies only to black bodies. ✅ It applies to ALL bodies, with the modification $E = e\sigma T^4$ where $e$ is the emissivity. Real objects with $e < 1$ emit less than a black body at the same temperature.  ·  ❌ A body at thermal equilibrium radiates no energy. ✅ A body at thermal equilibrium radiates energy continuously, but it also ABSORBS exactly the same amount of energy from its surroundings. The NET radiation is zero — not the radiation itself.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The Stefan-Boltzmann law was discovered by Boltzmann alone. ✅ Josef Stefan proposed it empirically in 1879. Ludwig Boltzmann derived it theoretically in 1884. Both are credited for the law.  ·  ❌ The Stefan-Boltzmann law applies only to radiation — it has no analog in conduction or convection. ✅ The concept of thermal radiation power ($P = e\sigma A T^4$) has NO analog in conduction or convection because those mechanisms depend on temperature DIFFERENCE ($\Delta T$), not absolute $T^4$.  ·  Note 3: Practice numerical problems regularly for mastery of Stefan-Boltzmann Law
